subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which trial in 1925 pitted the teaching of evolution against religious fundamentalism?
questions.explain: The Scopes Trial saw a teacher prosecuted for teaching evolution in Tennessee.

questions.q: In which year did the Wall Street Crash occur, signalling the start of the Great Depression?
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash took place in October 1929.

questions.q: Which infamous Chicago gangster dominated the bootlegging trade during Prohibition?
questions.explain: Al Capone ran a violent bootlegging empire in Chicago during Prohibition.

questions.q: Which 1935 law gave American workers the right to join trade unions and bargain collectively?
questions.explain: The 1935 Wagner Act guaranteed workers' rights to unionise and bargain collectively.

questions.q: Which 1933 measure shut the banks temporarily to restore confidence at the start of the New Deal?
questions.explain: FDR declared a bank holiday and passed the Emergency Banking Act in March 1933 to stabilise banks.

questions.q: What was the name of FDR's programme of relief, recovery and reform launched from 1933?
questions.explain: Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal aimed to combat the Great Depression.

questions.q: Which Alphabet Agency built dams to provide electricity and jobs in a poor river valley?
questions.explain: The Tennessee Valley Authority built dams to generate power and create work in the 1930s.

questions.q: Which 1920 amendment to the US Constitution gave American women the right to vote?
questions.explain: The 19th Amendment, ratified in 1920, granted women the vote across the USA.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment introduced Prohibition, banning the sale of alcohol from 1920?
questions.explain: The 18th Amendment brought in Prohibition in 1920; the 21st repealed it in 1933.

questions.q: Which 1933 agency paid farmers to reduce production in order to raise crop prices?
questions.explain: The Agricultural Adjustment Administration (AAA) of 1933 paid farmers to cut output and lift prices.

questions.q: Which Alphabet Agency paid young men to work on conservation projects such as planting trees?
questions.explain: The Civilian Conservation Corps gave unemployed young men conservation work.

questions.q: Which 1920s 'Red Scare' case saw two Italian immigrant anarchists controversially executed?
questions.explain: Sacco and Vanzetti were executed in 1927 amid anti-immigrant and anti-radical feeling.

questions.q: What nickname was given to the shanty towns of the unemployed that sprang up during the Great Depression?
questions.explain: The shanty towns were mockingly called 'Hoovervilles' after President Hoover, who was blamed for the slump.

questions.q: Who was US President when the Wall Street Crash and early Great Depression occurred?
questions.explain: Herbert Hoover was president from 1929 and was blamed for the Depression.

questions.q: In which year was Prohibition repealed, ending the national ban on alcohol?
questions.explain: Prohibition was repealed in 1933 by the 21st Amendment.

questions.q: FDR reassured Americans through informal radio broadcasts known as what?
questions.explain: From 1933 Roosevelt used 'fireside chats' on the radio to explain his New Deal and restore confidence.

questions.q: Which 1924 law sharply restricted immigration into the USA using a quota system favouring northern Europeans?
questions.explain: The 1924 National Origins Act set quotas that heavily restricted southern and eastern European immigration.

questions.q: What term describes the policy of buying goods now and paying in instalments, common in the 1920s boom?
questions.explain: Buying on credit (hire purchase) let consumers buy cars and goods by paying in instalments.

questions.q: The 'Hundred Days' in 1933 refers to the burst of legislation early in whose presidency?
questions.explain: FDR pushed many laws through Congress in his first hundred days in office in 1933.

questions.q: Which industrialist pioneered the moving assembly line that made the Model T affordable to ordinary Americans?
questions.explain: Henry Ford's assembly line slashed production costs and made the Model T a mass-market car.

questions.q: Roosevelt won the 1932 presidential election against which incumbent Republican?
questions.explain: FDR defeated the sitting president Herbert Hoover in the 1932 election amid the Depression.

questions.q: In which year did the Wall Street boom peak before share prices collapsed in the Crash?
questions.explain: Share prices peaked in the summer of 1929 before the October Wall Street Crash.
